other_failure_modes.name: OOF Leakage via Early Stopping
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses the validation fold for early stopping and then uses the predictions from the exact same validation fold as out-of-fold (OOF) predictions for the ensemble. This leaks information because the OOF predictions are optimistically biased, leading to suboptimal ensemble weights.

other_failure_modes.name: Test Set Data Leakage via Imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Missing values in the test set are imputed using the test set's own median rather than the training set's median. In a real-world setting, test data should be imputed using statistics learned solely from the training set.
other_failure_modes.evidence: combined_df = combined_df.fillna(combined_df.median())  # applied independently to test_df in X_test_df = engineer_features(test_df, ...)

other_failure_modes.name: Cross-validation Leakage via Pre-CV Imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Missing values in the training set are imputed using the overall training set's median before cross-validation splitting, leaking validation fold statistics into the training folds.
other_failure_modes.evidence: X_train_df = engineer_features(train_df, raw_feature_cols) ... for fold, (train_idx, val_idx) in enumerate(skf.split(X_train_raw, y_train)):

summary: The agent provides an excellent and highly sophisticated solution, including extensive feature engineering, rigorous CV, and a carefully optimized ensemble using Nelder-Mead. However, it exhibits a common Kaggle anti-pattern where out-of-fold predictions are generated on the same validation data used for early stopping, leading to biased meta-features. Additionally, it computes imputation statistics (median) on the test set directly and on the full training set before CV splitting, causing data leakage.
